jobs.description: Employer: Foot Locker Corporate Expires: 10/16/2026 THIS IS NOT A REMOTE ROLEFoot Locker, Inc. is a leading footwear and apparel retailer that unlocks the “inner sneakerhead” in all of us. With approximately 2,500 retail stores in 26 countries across North America, Europe, Asia, Australia, and New Zealand, and a licensed store presence in the Middle East and Asia, Foot Locker, Inc. has a strong history of sneaker authority that sparks discovery and ignites the power of sneaker culture through its portfolio of brands, including Foot Locker, Kids Foot Locker, Champs Sports, WSS, and atmos. Foot Locker is looking for Interns to join the Supply Chain team in Junction City, Kansas. The Supply Chain team is a high functioning team with expertise in inventory management, logistics, and cross functional partnerships that ensures the right products reach the right places at the right time, driving customer satisfaction and business growth. Working with cross-functional teams, the Supply Chain Quality Internship role will support the Quality Assurance (QA) and Inventory Control (IC) teams in conducting various quality assurance activities, including product assessment, process monitoring, and data analysis. This internship provides an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in quality management systems, compliance, and continuous improvement processes.Responsibilities • Summer program located at one of Foot Locker’s Distribution Centers working closely with team members and leaders to develop an understanding Quality Assurance and Inventory Control within the distribution centers.• Assist in conducting inspections and audits of products, processes, and materials to ensure compliance with quality standards and specifications.• Support the creation, implementation, and maintenance of quality procedures, guidelines, and documentation.• Perform data collection and analysis related to product defects, trends, and improvement opportunities.• Participate in root cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions (CAPA) for non-conforming products or processes.• Collaborate with cross-functional teams including manufacturing, engineering, and supply chain to resolve quality issues.• Support the preparation of reports, summaries, and presentations for internal stakeholders.• Assist in the development and improvement of quality control processes and testing methods.• Participate in quality improvement projects and initiatives aimed at increasing product reliability and reducing waste.• Other duties as assigned.Qualifications To qualify for an internship with Foot Locker, individuals must:• Undergraduate or graduate business student pursuing a degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Industrial Engineering, or related field.• 3.2 GPA• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.• Attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy in testing and data collection.• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).• A proactive and self-motivated approach to learning and tasks.• Basic understanding of quality tools and methodologies (e.g., Six Sigma, ISO standards, SPC) is a plus.• Effective communication skills for all levels of the organization• Ability to work cross-functionally• Willingness to learn with hands-on experience• Proficient with Microsoft Office Tools: Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. jobs.title: Finance or Accounting Intern at Haworth
jobs.description: Employer: Haworth Expires: 10/16/2026 Job Title: Finance or Accounting InternPosting Start Date: 9/15/26 Company OverviewAt Haworth, we're not just creating office furniture; we're shaping dynamic workspaces. As a global leader in workspace solutions, we're on a journey to redefine the future of work. Our headquarters in Holland, MI, is the hub of innovation, and we are excited to bring on our summer 2027 intern cohort to help continue driving creativity and progress. Why Haworth:Culture of Innovation: Join a company that values innovation and empowers its employees to think outside the box.Hands-On Experience: Gain real-world skills through meaningful projects and work directly with teams across departments. Career Growth: Test drive a career in your field and learn from professionals. Build your network, skills and resume. Haworth is a global leader in workspace design, with a legacy of innovation spanning over 70 years. As a family-owned business, Haworth maintains the agility and customer-focus of a smaller company while designing and manufacturing products that are distributed worldwide. Interns join one of Haworth's dedicated product, manufacturing, or service teams, gaining hands-on experience working directly with industry experts. Projects provide exposure to Haworth's full portfolio, from award-winning furniture to architectural interior products and comprehensive workspace solutions. Haworth's culture is defined by connectivity, collaboration, and continual learning. We foster a work environment where employees actively engage with our spaces and products. Our headquarters doubles as a dynamic showroom, where many dealers and customers visit to experience our designs firsthand. This unique environment allows you to interact directly with the spaces and furniture you help create, fostering a deeper connection to your work and the impact it has on our clients. Job Overview We are currently looking for paid Finance or Accounting Interns to join our team in Holland, Michigan. This position will be working onsite at the Haworth Corporate Headquarters. As a Finance or Accounting Intern, with a focused area in Finance, Accounting or Tax, you will participate in a carefully designed internship program that will provide you with meaningful work and learning opportunities. You will also have an opportunity to work with multiple functional groups within Finance and Accounting assisting with financial and data analysis, research, system administration, process improvement and a variety of other projects and assignments. These experiences may also introduce you to new tools, technologies, and ways of working. Get ready for an adventurous summer as a Haworth intern! You'll join a cohort of around 50 other dynamic interns for a 12-week program packed with hands-on learning. After a few weeks of work you’ll be attending NeoCon, the largest commercial design event in the world. There you will see an insider's look at all the latest industry trends and innovations. Throughout the summer you will own real projects that will give you a taste of what it's like to work in a leading business and manufacturing environment. Each week offers new experiences for our intern cohort. You will have opportunities to sharpen your skills through global learning workshops, networking with other interns and Haworth members, presenting before large audiences, and using your educational foundation in a business environment. You will also gain exposure to new tools, technologies, and business processes. By the end of the summer, you'll leave with real skills, an expanded professional network, and great memories. jobs.title: Culinary Internship, Eurest at Compass Group USA
jobs.description: Employer: Compass Group USA - Eurest Expires: 10/17/2026 Eurest Culinary Internship: OVERVIEW: The Eurest Culinary Internship Program is a paid, immersive learning experience designed for students pursuing careers in culinary arts, hospitality, event management, food service, and business operations. Interns have the opportunity to work within a dynamic and inspirational hospitality culture while gaining firsthand experience at one of the nation's leading foodservice and hospitality organizations. For more than 50 years, Eurest has partnered with more than 58% of the Fortune 100 companies across a wide range of industries, delivering restaurant-quality dining and hospitality experiences in corporate and office environments. Working alongside chefs and culinary leaders, interns gain firsthand experience in the daily operations of a professional kitchen. Interns will learn and support food preparation, recipe execution, station setup, service production, inventory organization, receiving deliveries, quality control, and food safety practices. Throughout the summer, participants are treated as an extension of the culinary team, developing an understanding of how preparation, teamwork, and execution come together to deliver exceptional dining experiences. This 10-week internship is intentionally structured to provide:70% Hands-On Experience: Learning by doing through department/station rotations, event support, operational projects, and real business challenges.20% Mentorship & Career Development: Personalized coaching, leadership shadowing, and guidance from experienced culinary professionals.10% Cohort Learning & Networking: Weekly professional development sessions led by company leaders and industry experts. INTERSHIP JOURNEY: Weeks 1-2: Foundation & Onboarding - Complete orientation, facility tours, and department introductions.Learn company standards, service excellence practices, and operational procedures.Build relationships with leaders and team members across the business.Gain an understanding of how hospitality, events, and client services work together to create exceptional experiences. Weeks 3-8: Management Team Rotations - Interns become an extension of the management team and rotate through key areas of the business, gaining exposure to the day-to-day responsibilities of the culinary team. Throughout the rotations, interns will:Prepare menu items and support daily food production across various kitchen stations, including grill, deli, pizza/pasta, salad bar, and international cuisine. Assist with catering and special events, from preparation and set up to execution. Engage with guests while delivering exceptional hospitality and accommodating dietary needs. Learn and apply culinary, customer service, food safety, and sanitation standards. Participate in leadership meetings and weekly debriefs to gain insight into kitchen operations, departmental goals, and business performance. Build professional relationships while developing teamwork, communication, and leadership skills. Weeks 8-10: Capstone Project - During the final weeks of the program, interns will apply everything they've learned by leading a project in an area of the business that aligns with their interests and career goals. This project provides an opportunity to make a meaningful impact while showcasing skills developed throughout the internship experience. Internship candidates must meet the criteria below to be eligible for the Culinary Internship Experience Program:Applicants must be currently enrolled in a college or professional culinary programMeet university’s GPA requirement for internshipSuccessful completion of sanitation standards trainingSuccessful completion of relevant knife skills and/or Intro to Culinary courseworkMust be available to work 20 - 40 hours a week based on business needs & internship requirementsCollege credit is not required, but we will provide appropriate documentation if necessary.

The 127th U.S. Open Championship will be held at Pebble Beach Golf Links, located in Pebble Beach, CA. This will be the seventh U.S. Open Championship hosted by Pebble Beach. This historic site has held a variety of major events that include a U.S. Women’s Open, U.S Amateur, and U.S. Women’s Amateur. The last time the U.S. Open Championship took place at Pebble Beach was in 2019. The 2027 U.S. Open Long-Term Operations Administrative Internship offers an exciting opportunity to gain hands-on experience in sports management while contributing to the planning and execution of one of golf's most prestigious events. This internship provides the opportunity to work alongside industry professionals, develop valuable operational skills, and gain firsthand insight into the preparation required to deliver a world-class sporting event. About this role: The Long-Term Operations Administrative Intern assists the United States Golf Association with the operations of the 2027 U.S. Open Championship, including advance set-up, Championship week responsibilities and post-Championship breakdown. This is a paid internship, with a housing stipend provided. Working at the U.S. Open, you will experience a fast-paced work environment. The successful candidate must have the ability to work under pressure and handle multiple tasks at one time. Each day brings new challenges, and this position requires top-notch organizational and communication skills. In this position, the Operations Administrative intern will typically work in an office environment as well as at the course, as required. The Operations Administrative intern must have the ability to handle physical tasks such as lifting boxes and furniture and perform manual labor; spending extensive time in the sun and/or inclement weather should be expected. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: 2027 Summer Associate (Intern) at BRG
jobs.description: Employer: BRG Expires: 10/17/2026 We Do Consulting Differently Berkeley Research Group (BRG) is a global consulting firm that helps its clients, which consist of leading organizations and businesses, advance in three key areas: disputes and investigations, corporate finance, and performance improvement and advisory. We are an integrated group of experts, industry leaders, academics, data scientists, and economists, working beyond borders and disciplines. We harness our collective expertise to deliver the inspired insights and practical strategies our clients need to stay ahead of what’s next. About the Role The work of a Summer Associate can have quantitative and qualitative aspects, depending on the needs of specific projects and the Summer Associate’s skills and interests. Projects range from subject matter research to data collection, to the preparation of economic, statistical, financial, and other forms of analysis. You will build technical skills and contribute to work that shapes important legal and business outcomes. The Summer Associate program will be approximately 8 weeks long and begin in Summer 2027. We’re committed to helping our Summer Associates succeed by providing them with dedicated mentors, training programs, hands-on learning opportunities and support from industry experts. Our Summer Associate program is a pipeline program, and we aim to convert Summer Associates to full-time Associates after graduation, assuming the role is a fit on both ends. What You’ll Do Develop a practical understanding of industries, markets, legal claims, and business issues relevant to each engagement by gathering and reviewing information from our clients and their business, academic literature, legal documents, specialized industry resources, commercial databases, or other sources appropriate for the unique requirements of a project. Identify, collect, develop, maintain, analyze and review data, qualitative materials, spreadsheets and other files as dictated by complex project needs. Combine programming, model building, and statistical analysis skills using relational database and statistical programs to analyze a variety of subjects with software such as SQL, R, Stata, SAS, Python, or Snowflake. Interact with senior staff, experts, and clients to clearly communicate questions, findings, economic and business concepts, and recommendations. Demonstrate creativity and efficient analytical skills to develop novel solutions tailored to unique projects. Provide valuable contributions to client deliverables and expert reports. Qualifications Progression towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, Accounting, Business, Finance, Healthcare Administration or a related analytical field, with an expected graduation date between Winter 2027 and Summer 2028.3.6 GPA or higher preferred. Demonstrated interest in applying analytics to business, financial, legal, regulatory, or policy questions. Strong quantitative, research, problem-solving, and written communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, client-service environment. Attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to producing high-quality work. Experience with statistical, econometric and programming tools such as Excel, Stata, R, Python, SQL or similar platforms is preferred. Fluency with AI tools is desirable. Candidates must be able to submit verification of their legal right to work in the United States, without company sponsorship now or in the future. Our Practice Areas Summer Associates are hired to support project work aligned to one of BRG’s practice areas, though there may be flexibility to work across multiple practice areas. Candidates can select a preferred practice area as part of the application process. You can find more information about them below. 1. Antitrust & Competition: Experts in our antitrust practice apply learning from industrial organization, econometrics and microeconomic theory to provide testimony to counsel, corporations, and governments in matters involving antitrust litigation and merger reviews. Our experts and academic affiliates have testified in some of the largest and most significant antitrust matters of the past two decades, including antitrust actions involving platforms and multi-sided markets, automobile manufacturers, insurance companies, financial markets (e.g., LIBOR and foreign exchange) and other industries. Our project teams frequently evaluate industry conduct and assess antitrust liability, calculate damages from anticompetitive conduct and build simulation models to understand the impacts of proposed mergers. 2. Business Insurance Claims (BIC): We provide immediate and strategic guidance to policyholders following a catastrophe. Our BIC experts meticulously analyze financial data and operational records, develop robust financial models, and prepare comprehensive, well-documented insurance claims, accelerating resolution and maximizing claim payments. 3. Construction: We specialize in data analytics, litigation support, claims/dispute analysis, scheduling/logistics management and expert witness testimony within the construction, engineering, and architectural fields. Our team supports clients through budget and payment advisory, loss assessment and valuation, estimations and takeoffs, and insurance and damages claim valuations. We also specialize in providing our clients with budgetary and payment oversight, project management recommendations, project scheduling generation, and constructability and viability analyses for both upcoming and ongoing construction projects. 4. Commercial Disputes: We combine exceptional analytical and accounting skills and industry-specific knowledge to provide comprehensive support throughout the legal process. From initial case assessment and in-depth damages analysis to litigation support and expert testimony in hearings, trials, arbitration, regulatory proceedings, and mediation, we deliver data-driven insights to secure favorable outcomes. 5. Consumer Protection, Product Liability & Environment: Our experts are regularly engaged in matters involving claims of consumer fraud, product liability, false advertising, data privacy and data breach, and alleged violations of environmental and natural resource law. Associates in this area employ techniques from microeconomic theory, econometrics, marketing and environmental and resource economics to address in class certification, liability and damages. 6. Energy & Climate: We help clients across the global energy value chain address complex strategic, commercial, financial, market, regulatory, and dispute-related issues. Our work spans power and utilities, oil and gas, renewables, storage, advanced nuclear, eMobility, hydrogen and low-carbon fuels, carbon management, infrastructure, and the broader energy transition. We conduct rigorous market research, economic modeling, and detailed reporting, helping clients address legal and business challenges. 7. Financial Institutions Advisory: We are a trusted advisor to leading financial services companies. We work to help clients meet and execute strategies related to risk and regulation, compliance, financial crime, innovations in technology, accounting, cryptocurrency and blockchain, business process outsourcing, the Bank Secrecy Act, anti-money laundering, lookbacks, data quality, and evolving customer experience expectations. 8. Healthcare Advisory: As healthcare organizations navigate increasing reimbursement pressure, workforce challenges, regulatory and enforcement complexity, and rapid technological change, we work alongside executive teams and governing bodies to identify opportunities, implement practical solutions, and deliver measurable, lasting results. Our integrated team combines deep industry expertise across strategy, revenue management, operational excellence, clinical transformation, and technology and AI with the comprehensive capabilities of a global advisory firm and the agility, senior attention, and client service of a boutique consultancy. 9. Healthcare Analytics and Disputes: We tackle complex legal and operational challenges in the healthcare industry using data-driven, objective, and innovative approaches. Our experts lead advisory, risk management, and litigation matters, combining deep healthcare industry expertise with cutting edge research, analytics and financial modeling. 10. Intellectual Property: Our intellectual property experts and academic affiliates regularly testify on damages, trademark confusion, irreparable harm and commercial success. Many of our matters require expertise in consumer behavior, judgment and decision-making and our project teams work on some of the world's largest patent infringement, trademark infringement, trade secret misappropriation, and copyright infringement cases. Associates in this practice regularly build econometric models of market prices, analyze survey data and the results of choice experiments and assist with the preparation of expert reports and other client deliverables. Locations Summer Associates will primarily be hired in locations like Boston, Washington DC, Chicago, New York, Houston, Los Angeles and the San Francisco Bay Area. There are also a limited number of opportunities in smaller offices like Tampa and Pittsburgh. Summer Associates are expected to work in the office five days per week to take full advantage of the mentorship, collaboration, and relationship-building opportunities that support their professional growth. Remote roles for practices that require frequent travel to client sites are also available. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit a copy of their resume, cover letter and transcript through the job posting. You can find the job application deadlines listed below:Deadline for priority review: September 5Deadline for secondary review: September 19Deadline for final review: October 16 When applying, please answer the questionnaire to indicate your location and practice area preferences. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. A member of the recruiting team will be in touch if there is an interest in scheduling interviews. Salary Range: $25/hour - $40/hour Global Competition Review recently recognized BRG as an Outstanding firm in GCR 100: Economics 2025, which ranks the world’s leading economic consultancies. Consulting Magazine recognized BRG as a Best Firms to Work for in 2025. BRG is a recipient of the Human Rights Campaigns Equality 100 Award for our LGBTQ+ corporate policies, practices and beliefs. About BRG BRG combines world-leading academic credentials with world-tested business expertise and purpose-built emerging technologies. Our culture centers on agility and connectivity which sets us apart and gets you ahead. At BRG, our professionals include specialist consultants, industry experts, renowned academics, and leading-edge data scientists. Together, they bring a diversity of real-world experience, data, and human and artificial intelligence, to economics, disputes, and investigations; corporate finance; and performance improvement services that address the most complex challenges facing organizations across the globe. Our unique structure nurtures the interdisciplinary relationships that give us the edge, laying the groundwork for more informed insights and more original, incisive thinking. When paired with our global reach and resources, our diverse perspectives and technical capabilities make us uniquely capable to address our clients’ challenges. We get results because we know how to apply our thinking to your world. At BRG, we don’t just show you what’s possible. We’re built to help you make it happen. BRG is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our hiring practices provide equal opportunity for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender, national origin, age, United States military veteran status, ancestry, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, medical condition including genetic characteristics or information, veteran status, or mental or physical disability so long as the essential functions of the job can be performed with or without reasonable accommodation, or any other protected category under federal, state, or local law.

Demonstrated ability to follow and execute detailed plans – able to anticipate and analyze problems and provide logical solutions. Ability to work well under pressure. Professional demeanor.This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Interns may perform other duties as assigned.The USGA is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Assistant Examiner Intern at Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Expires: 10/17/2026 About the Opportunity The Richmond Fed Supervision, Regulation, and Credit (SRC) department is now hiring for our 2027 Summer Internship Program. SRC is responsible for the supervision of bank holding companies, state member banks, and foreign banking organizations. Supervision is completed from two differing aspects, safety and soundness (assessing a bank’s financial performance and risk to the FDIC insurance fund) and consumer compliance (assessing a bank’s compliance with consumer guidelines such as Fair Lending and Community Reinvestment Act). SRC is also responsible for Discount Window operations where money can be lent to organizations in need of funding. The Assistant Examiner Internship Program provides a unique experience to explore SRC’s supervision business lines and will be located in Richmond, VA. The program provides summer interns with the opportunity to enhance essential business skills and increase understanding of the Federal Reserve’s role in the supervision of financial institutions. During the program, you will gain exposure to the supervisory process through bank examination participation. While participating on bank examinations, you will interact with management at supervised institutions, review reports, participate in meetings, and assess risk exposures. You may review topics ranging from adequacy of risk management practices, operational controls, financial condition, and/or compliance with banking laws and regulations. In addition, you will participate in foundational learning, develop a relationship with a mentor, create and deliver presentations, and complete a final project As part of the Bank’s larger intern cohort, you will participate in professional development activities and be provided with an extensive understanding of the work of the Federal Reserve. In addition to specific business area tasks, you will receive leadership training, mentorship and valuable networking opportunities. What You Will Do: Rotate through three supervision business lines. Participate in an examination at the Federal Reserve Bank and/or a state member bank. Communicate findings and conclusions of supervisory activities to examination staff and senior management. Responsibly handle highly sensitive and confidential information. Observe and participate in relevant meetings to gain an extensive overview of the department and critical examination issues. Participate in a bank simulation exercise. Work with other interns to create and deliver a presentation to SRC related to internship experience. Qualifications: Rising senior with a minimum 3.3 GPA with a preferred emphasis in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or related field. Strong project management skills, including organization, planning and execution, analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work effectively in a team environment. Intellectual curiosity with willingness to ask questions. Other Requirements and Considerations: An applicant posting for employment as a Federal Reserve examiner intern must be a U.S. citizen or hold a permanent residence visa/Green Card and be an intending citizen. Sponsorship or practical training extensions are not available for this position. Under conflicts of interest guidelines administered by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, examining personnel may not participate on an examination of a financial institution or affiliate if the examiner was employed by the financial institution or affiliate within the past 12 months. Please review the Bank’s Code of Conduct to ensure compliance with conflicts of interest rules and personal investment restrictions. The Code is available on the About Us, Careers webpage at www.richmondfed.org. FRB ethics rules generally prohibit employees and their immediate families from owning investments in banks, savings associations or their holding companies (Section 5.3). Additionally, employees engaged in Supervision and Regulation may be subject to borrowing and deposit restrictions. These employees may need to recuse themselves from certain supervisory work based on: their borrowing relationships if a financial institution employs a member of the employee’s immediate family if the individual was employed by the financial institution or affiliate within the past 12 months In certain cases, the recusal may be so extensive it could materially reduce the effectiveness of the prospective employee. Selected candidate is subject to special background check procedures. The hourly rate for summer interns is $23.50/hour. jobs.title: Summer Intern 2027 - Retirement Sales at John Hancock
jobs.description: Employer: John Hancock Expires: 10/17/2026 At Manulife John Hancock, we believe in investing in the future – starting with you. Our Retirement Sales Internship Program is your launchpad to success, offering the support, structure, and exciting opportunities you need to thrive and make your mark. This internship program provides students with an immersive professional learning experience in retirement sales at John Hancock. Designed to build a pipeline of future talent, this program exposes interns to sales strategy, financial products, and client engagement while working alongside Internal Sales leadership and business partners. Students will gain practical knowledge of investments and sales systems, sharpen their professional skills, and expand their networks across the organization. Position Responsibilities Learn foundational industry knowledge including investments, financial products, privacy/compliance, and the John Hancock business model. Strong communication, organization, and time management skills. Preferred Qualifications Prior internship, co-op, or work experience in financial services, sales, or client-facing roles. Familiarity with CRM tools such as Salesforce or other sales enablement platforms. Demonstrated leadership experience through prior roles, campus involvement, or extracurricular activities. Ability to learn quickly, work independently, and adapt in a fast-paced environment. Positive attitude, enthusiasm for client engagement, and strong relationship-building skills. When you join our team: We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want. We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words. As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see. As part of our internship program, you will gain early access to Manulife John Hancock’s premier early talent program, GRO, tailored to graduating students! This program is designed to launch your career with the support, structure, and opportunities you need to thrive.
